A method to initialize the neural point cloud and their features for Point-NeRF using an external point cloud reconstruction (specifically COLMAP).
It solves the problem of how to provide initial positions, variances, and feature vectors for the neural points.
The variance parameter $\gamma_i$ for each point $p_i$ is initialized to 0.3.
To acquire the feature vector $f_i$ for a point $p_i$, views where the point is occluded are ruled out, and the view where the camera is closest to the point is selected.
The point is unprojected onto the feature maps extracted by the Image Feature Extraction 2D CNN (Gf) from the selected closest view to obtain $f_i$.
Leaf nodes contain the full set of optimized Gaussian properties (base color, SH coefficients, position, covariance).
Initializes a single ellipsoid from a set of 3D points using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to determine orientation, center, and radii.
The minimum allowed radius $r_{\min}$ is typically 0.005 to avoid numerical problems.
Aggregates filtered multiview depth maps from an MVS method into a unified 3D point cloud.
An initial optimization phase prunes noisy Gaussians by freezing Gaussian centers and optimizing other parameters for $N_{prun}$ iterations, removing Gaussians with opacity $\alpha_k < \tau$.
Initializes the base feature $f_{base}$ and directional feature $f_{dir}$ with the RGB color values of the corresponding SfM points.
The MVS point cloud is generated in the same coordinate system as the SfM reconstruction used to initialize 3DGS, allowing direct comparison with Gaussian centers.
Initializes each image volume with 50,000 Gaussians.
The background threshold is 0.05, and the intensity initialization coefficient $c_i$ is 0.15.
*   **Time Complexity:** SfM initialization is significantly slower than random initialization due to the feature matching and triangulation steps.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Linear in the number of points $N$.
*   **When to Use:** Use SfM initialization when 2D images are available and sufficient feature matches can be found.
